fullPassage: Resilience: The Power to Overcome City Wellness Center Newsletter This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity. This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events. There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back. You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people.” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity! Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. It works like this. Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad. Proceed with what you were doing. Or start something different based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life. Third, be connected. Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors. Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength. Good communication helps resilience. This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks. I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. Remember that there is no better time to build your “resilience muscle” than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty. Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger. However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges. Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones. Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges. So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life.

questions.passage: Whatever life path we ①<u>choose</u>, we all experience adversity.  This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② overcoming → to overcome: 명사 ability 뒤에는 to부정사가 와서 '~할 능력'이 되므로 to overcome
det.analysis:
① choose: 'Whatever life path we choose'는 '우리가 어떤 삶의 길을 선택하든'이에요. whatever절 안에서 주어 we의 동사로 choose가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② overcoming → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'we all need the ability overcoming difficulties'는 '우리 모두는 어려움을 극복할 능력이 필요하다'라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 명사 ability(능력)는 'the ability to + 동사원형(~할 능력)' 형태로 to부정사의 꾸밈을 받아요. 그래서 overcoming이 아니라 to overcome으로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ overcoming은 틀림 ←정답

③ springing: 'Resilience means springing back'은 '회복탄력성은 다시 튀어 오르는 것을 뜻한다'예요. mean(~을 뜻하다) 뒤에 '~하는 것'이라는 내용이 올 때는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰니 springing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ to handle: 'the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events'는 '어려운 인생의 사건들을 다루고, 회복하고, 그로부터 득을 얻는 능력'이에요. 명사 ability 뒤 to부정사라 to handle이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: the ability to + 동사원형 = ~할 능력 (명사 뒤 to부정사)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ understood → understanding: not A but B 병렬 구조에서 A(being passive)와 형태를 맞춘 동명사 understanding
det.analysis:
① respect: 'accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life'는 '역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이고 존중하라'예요. 명령문에서 accept와 and로 이어진 동사원형 respect가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② being passive: 'This doesn't mean being passive'는 '이것은 수동적으로 있으라는 뜻이 아니다'예요. mean 뒤에 '~하는 것'은 동명사로 쓰니 being passive가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ understood → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'This doesn't mean being passive, but understood that ~'은 'not A but B(A가 아니라 B)' 구조예요. A 자리가 동명사 being passive이니, B 자리도 형태를 맞춰 동명사 understanding이어야 해요. 과거분사 understood를 쓰면 병렬이 깨져 문장이 성립하지 않아요. 그래서 understanding으로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ understood는 틀림 ←정답

④ could never have happened: 'success stories that could never have happened without adversity'는 '역경이 없었다면 결코 일어날 수 없었을 성공담들'이에요. '조동사 과거형 + have + p.p.'로 과거 일에 대한 추측을 나타내니 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: not A but B 병렬 = A와 B의 형태를 맞춘다: being ↔ understanding

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ help → helps: 주어가 동명사구 Practicing resilience during tough times(단수 취급)이므로 단수 동사 helps
det.analysis:
① whom: 'people whom you can trust'는 '당신이 신뢰할 수 있는 사람들'이에요. 뒤 절에서 trust의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사 whom이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② why: 'This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks'는 '이것이 회복탄력성 있는 사람들이 좋은 지원망을 만드는 경향이 있는 이유다'예요. 선행사 the reason 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오니 관계부사 why가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ the moment when: 'no better time ~ than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity'는 '역경의 한가운데에 있는 바로 그 순간'이에요. 시간 선행사 the moment 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오니 관계부사 when이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ help → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Practicing resilience during tough times help you endure and grow stronger'에서 주어는 'Practicing resilience during tough times(힘든 시기에 회복탄력성을 연습하는 것)'라는 동명사구예요. 동명사구 주어는 단수로 취급하므로 동사도 단수형 helps를 써야 해요. 주어와 동사 사이에 수식어가 길게 끼어 있어 헷갈리기 쉽지만, during tough times는 수식어일 뿐이에요. ❌ help는 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: 동명사구 주어(Practicing ~)는 단수 취급 → 단수 동사(helps)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① full of → free from: '어떤 삶도 문제로부터 자유롭지 않다', 즉 누구나 역경을 겪는다는 흐름이라 free from
det.analysis:
① full of → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'No life is free from problems(어떤 삶도 문제로부터 자유롭지 않다)'예요. 바로 뒤에 '어떤 길을 가든 우리 모두 역경을 겪는다'가 이어지니, '문제가 없는 삶은 없다'는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 'No life is full of problems(어떤 삶도 문제로 가득하지 않다)'라고 하면 '누구도 문제를 겪지 않는다'는 정반대 뜻이 되어 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

② difficulties: 'the ability to overcome difficulties'는 '어려움을 극복하는 능력'이에요. 역경을 이겨 내는 힘을 설명하는 흐름이라 '어려움(difficulties)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

③ bouncy: 'just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground'는 '땅에 부딪힌 뒤의 탱탱볼처럼'이에요. 다시 튀어 오르는(springing back) 모습을 비유하니 '잘 튀는(bouncy)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ quickly: 'you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times'는 '힘든 시간들로부터 다시 튀어 올라 빠르게 회복할 수 있다'예요. 회복탄력성의 핵심이 빠른 회복이라 quickly가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 뒤 문장 '우리 모두 역경을 겪는다' → 문제로부터 '자유로운(free from)' 삶은 없다

Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger.  However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ more → less: 회복탄력성 있는 사람들은 실패나 도전을 '덜(less)' 두려워하기 때문에 더 행복하다는 흐름
det.analysis:
① remove: 'these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering'은 '이 전략들이 쉽다거나 모든 스트레스와 고통을 없애 준다(고 말하는 것이 아니다)'예요. '없애다(remove)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② urge: 'I urge you to practice them whenever you can'은 '할 수 있을 때마다 그것들을 연습하라고 강력히 권한다'예요. 필자가 전략 연습을 권하는 흐름이라 '강력히 권하다(urge)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ gradually: 'Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones'는 '그러면 점차 큰 어려움도 더 잘 다룰 수 있게 된다'예요. 작은 스트레스부터 연습해 서서히 성장한다는 흐름이라 '점차(gradually)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ more afraid → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges(회복탄력성 있는 사람들은 실패나 도전을 덜 두려워하기 때문에 더 행복하고 더 충만한 경향이 있다)'예요. '더 두려워해서(more afraid)' 더 행복하다는 것은 인과가 맞지 않아요. 두려움이 '적어야(less afraid)' 행복과 충만으로 이어져요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 더 행복한 이유 = 실패를 '덜(less)' 두려워하기 때문. 'more afraid'는 인과가 뒤집힘

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② quickly recover from a crisis(위기로부터 빠르게 회복하다): 우리 모두 회복탄력성의 잠재력을 갖고 태어났다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'we all can develop the strength to ___ that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health'(우리 모두는 그렇지 않으면 정신 건강에 지속적인 손상을 줄 수 있는 ___ 힘을 기를 수 있다). 앞에서 '우리는 모두 회복탄력성의 잠재력을 갖고 태어났다'고 했고, 이 글 전체가 역경에서 '다시 튀어 오르는' 힘을 말하고 있어요. 그러니 '위기로부터 빠르게 회복하는' 힘이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① ignore the pain caused by others(다른 사람들이 준 고통을 무시하다): 글은 고통을 무시하라는 것이 아니라 회복하라고 해요.

✅ ② quickly recover from a crisis(위기로부터 빠르게 회복하다): 회복탄력성 = 빠른 회복이라는 글의 핵심과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ blame ourselves for every failure(모든 실패에 대해 스스로를 탓하다): 자책은 글의 메시지와 정반대예요.

❌ ④ depend on others for every decision(모든 결정을 다른 사람에게 의존하다): 의존이 아니라 내면의 힘을 기르라는 글이에요.
det.tip: 글 전체 핵심 = 위기에서 '빠르게 회복하는(quickly recover)' 힘, 즉 회복탄력성

questions.passage: This is the real bouncing back.  You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people. ” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience.  Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① through practice(연습을 통해): 회복탄력성은 근육처럼 단련해 기를 수 있다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'You can build it up ___, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover'(생각, 행동, 습관을 길러서 ___ 그것을 키울 수 있다). 바로 앞에서 '회복탄력성은 근육과 같다'고 했어요. 근육은 꾸준한 단련, 즉 연습으로 키우는 것이고, 뒤에서도 '생각·행동·습관을 기른다'고 했으니 '연습을 통해'가 되어야 해요.

✅ ① through practice(연습을 통해): 근육 비유 + 습관 기르기와 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② by pure luck(순전히 운으로): 운이 아니라 스스로 기르는 것이라는 글의 핵심과 반대예요.

❌ ③ through medical treatment(의학적 치료를 통해): 치료는 언급되지 않았어요.

❌ ④ by avoiding stress(스트레스를 피함으로써): 글은 역경을 피하지 말고 받아들여 성장하라고 해요.
det.tip: resilience is like a muscle(근육) → 근육을 키우는 방법 = 연습(practice)

ch: through practice
by pure luck
through medical treatment
by avoiding stress

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문 근거: She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition
det.analysis:

❌ ② 원문은 'She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery'로, Mullins는 '태어날 때부터' 가진 질환 때문에 수술로 무릎 아래 두 다리를 잃었어요. 성인이 된 후의 사고가 아니에요.

✅ ③ 원문 'She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition'(그녀는 전국 대회에서 장애가 없는 선수들과 겨루었다)과 일치해요. ←정답

❌ ④ 원문은 'The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories'로, Andersen은 고난이 오히려 이야기를 쓰도록 영감을 준 '축복'이었다고 했어요. 방해가 아니에요.
det.tip: Mullins = 전국 대회에서 비장애 선수들과 경쟁 + 1996년 패럴림픽 참가

ch: Andersen은 유복했던 어린 시절의 경험 덕분에 유명한 이야기들을 쓸 수 있었다.

questions.passage: ” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life.  This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress.  Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me? ”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t.  Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process.  Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity!  Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself.  Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future.  Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문: This doesn't mean being passive — 받아들임은 수동적으로 있으라는 뜻이 아님
det.analysis:
❌ ① 이 진술은 일치해요. 원문 'First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life'(첫째, 역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이고 존중하라)와 맞아요.

✅ ② 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 원문은 'This doesn't mean being passive'(이것은 수동적으로 있으라는 뜻이 아니다)예요. 받아들임은 가만히 있는 것이 아니라, 바꿀 수 있는 것에 집중하고 도전을 배움의 과정으로 마주하는 거예요. ←정답

❌ ③ 이 진술은 일치해요. 원문 'have "me time," that is, personal time to look after yourself'(나만의 시간, 즉 자신을 돌보기 위한 개인적인 시간을 가져라)와 맞아요.

❌ ④ 이 진술은 일치해요. 원문 'be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future'(과거를 후회하지도 미래를 걱정하지도 말고 현재에 머물러라)와 맞아요.
det.tip: 함정: accept(받아들임) ≠ passive(수동적) — 원문이 직접 '수동적이라는 뜻이 아니다'라고 못 박음

ch: 첫 번째 전략은 역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이고 존중하는 것이다.
역경을 받아들이는 것은 아무 시도도 하지 않고 수동적으로 머무는 것을 의미한다.
'나만의 시간'은 자기 자신을 돌보기 위한 개인적인 시간을 뜻한다.
현재에 머무른다는 것은 과거를 후회하지도 미래를 걱정하지도 않는 것이다.

questions.passage: Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise.  If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique.  It works like this.  Stop whatever you are doing.  Take a few deep breaths.  Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad.  Proceed with what you were doing.  Or start something different based on what you observed.  Now go forward with your life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문 근거: Or start something different based on what you observed
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문의 첫 단계는 'Stop whatever you are doing'(하고 있던 일을 멈춰라)이고, 그다음이 'Take a few deep breaths'(심호흡을 몇 번 하라)예요. 호흡을 멈추는 것도, 생각을 비우는 것도 아니에요.

❌ ② 원문은 'Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad'(감정과 생각을 좋다 나쁘다 판단하지 말고 있는 그대로 관찰하라)예요. 즉시 판단하라는 것과 정반대예요.

❌ ③ 원문은 'Proceed with what you were doing. Or start something different'(하던 일을 계속하라. 또는 다른 일을 시작하라)로, 반드시 하던 일로만 돌아가야 하는 것이 아니에요.

✅ ④ 원문 'Or start something different based on what you observed'(또는 관찰한 것을 바탕으로 다른 일을 시작하라)와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: P 단계 = 하던 일 계속 or 관찰 결과에 따라 '다른 일' 시작 — 둘 다 가능

ch: STOP 기법의 첫 단계는 호흡을 완전히 멈추고 생각을 비우는 것이다.
감정을 관찰할 때는 그것이 좋은지 나쁜지를 즉시 판단해야 한다.
관찰을 마친 뒤에는 반드시 원래 하던 일로만 돌아가야 한다.
관찰한 것을 바탕으로 하던 일 대신 다른 일을 시작할 수도 있다.

This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress.  Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me? ”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself.  Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. questions.passage: Resilience: The Power to Overcome City Wellness Center Newsletter This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome. ” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength.  No life is free from problems.  Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity.  This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses.  To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience.  Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground.  If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity.  So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.  There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth.  Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories.  “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling. ” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity.  She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery.  She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996.  Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking.  She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential.  Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it.  This is the real bouncing back.  You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people. ” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience.  Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health.  The good news is that resilience is like a muscle.  You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events.  Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle. ” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life.  This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress.  Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me? ”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t.  Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process.  Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity!  Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself.  Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future.  Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise.  If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique.  It works like this.  Stop whatever you are doing.  Take a few deep breaths.  Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad.  Proceed with what you were doing.  Or start something different based on what you observed.  Now go forward with your life.  Third, be connected.  Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors.  Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength.  Good communication helps resilience.  This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks.  I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering.  Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress.  Remember that there is no better time to build your “resilience muscle” than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty.  Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger.  However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges.  Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones.  Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges.  So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ Bounce Back: Growing Stronger Through Hard Times(다시 튀어 오르기: 힘든 시간들을 통해 더 강해지기)
det.analysis:
글은 회복탄력성(resilience)이 무엇인지, 역경을 성장의 발판으로 삼은 사람들의 사례, 그리고 회복탄력성을 기르는 세 가지 전략을 차례로 설명하며 '역경에서 다시 튀어 올라 성장하라'고 말해요.

❌ ① How to Avoid Every Difficulty in Your Life(삶의 모든 어려움을 피하는 법): 글은 어려움을 피하라는 것이 아니라 받아들이고 극복하라고 해요. 정반대예요.

❌ ② The Secret Habits of Famous Writers and Athletes(유명 작가와 운동선수들의 비밀 습관): Andersen과 Mullins는 예시일 뿐, 글 전체의 중심이 아니에요.

✅ ③ Bounce Back: Growing Stronger Through Hard Times(다시 튀어 오르기: 힘든 시간들을 통해 더 강해지기): 회복탄력성의 정의, 사례, 전략까지 글 전체를 아우르는 제목이에요. ←정답

❌ ④ Meditation: The Only Cure for Modern Stress(명상: 현대 스트레스의 유일한 치료법): 명상은 여러 방법 중 하나로 잠깐 언급될 뿐이에요.

questions.passage: I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering.  Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress.  Remember that there is no better time to build your “resilience muscle” than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty.  Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger.  However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges.  Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones.  Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges.  So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ living a happy life(행복한 삶을 사는 것): 회복탄력성 있는 사람이 더 행복하고 충만하다는 앞 문장의 결론
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to ___'(그러므로 회복탄력성을 기르는 것은 역경을 극복하는 것뿐 아니라 ___의 열쇠이기도 하다). 바로 앞 문장에서 '회복탄력성 있는 사람들은 더 행복하고 더 충만한 경향이 있다(happier and more fulfilled)'고 했으니, 결론은 '행복한 삶을 사는 것'이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① removing all stress from your life(삶에서 모든 스트레스를 없애는 것): 앞에서 '이 전략들이 모든 스트레스를 없애 주는 것은 아니다'라고 분명히 했어요.

❌ ② avoiding every challenge in advance(모든 도전을 미리 피하는 것): 글은 도전을 피하지 말고 마주하라고 해요.

❌ ③ becoming a successful writer or athlete(성공한 작가나 운동선수가 되는 것): Andersen과 Mullins는 예시일 뿐, 결론이 아니에요.

✅ ④ living a happy life(행복한 삶을 사는 것): 'tend to be happier and more fulfilled'라는 앞 문장과 자연스럽게 이어지는 결론이에요. ←정답
det.tip: 앞 문장 'happier and more fulfilled(더 행복하고 충만한)' → 결론 = 행복한 삶(happy life)

ch: removing all stress from your life
avoiding every challenge in advance
becoming a successful writer or athlete
living a happy life

questions.passage: __________.  Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity.  This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses.  To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience.  Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground.  If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"어떤 삶도 문제로부터 자유롭지 않다." (6단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) free, from, is, life, No, problems 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: No life is free from problems
det.analysis:
'어떤 삶도 ~않다'는 'No + 명사'를 주어로 써서 나타내요: No life(어떤 삶도 ~않다). no가 명사 앞에 붙어 문장 전체를 부정해요.

동사는 is를 쓰고, '~로부터 자유로운'은 'free from + 명사'로 나타내요: is free from(~로부터 자유롭다).

무엇으로부터 자유롭지 않은가 하면 problems(문제들)예요.

순서대로 이으면 No / life / is / free / from / problems.
det.tip: No + 명사 주어 = 어떤 ~도 …않다 / be free from ~ = ~로부터 자유롭다

questions.wa: No life is free from problems
accept: No life is free from problems

questions.passage: Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. __________ (embrace) challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: embrace → Embracing: 문장의 주어 자리이므로 동명사 Embracing
det.analysis:
빈칸이 있는 문장은 '__________ challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process.'예요. '삶에서 도전과 예상치 못한 장애물을 받아들이는 것은 그것들을 배움의 과정으로 마주하도록 도와줄 수 있다'라는 뜻이에요.

이 문장의 동사는 can help이고, 그 앞 전체가 주어 자리예요. '받아들이는 것'이라는 명사 역할을 해야 하므로, 동사 embrace를 그대로 쓸 수 없고 동명사(-ing)로 바꿔야 해요.

그래서 Embracing(받아들이는 것)으로 고쳐 써야 해요. 'Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles'가 통째로 주어가 되고, 동명사구 주어라서 뒤에 단수 취급 동사가 와요.
det.tip: 문장 맨 앞 주어 자리의 동사 → 동명사(-ing)로: Embracing ~ = ~을 받아들이는 것

questions.passage: Third, be connected.  Allow yourself to __________, such as friends, family members, or counselors.  Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength.  Good communication helps resilience.  This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks.  I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering.  Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress.

다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.

"당신이 신뢰할 수 있는 사람들로부터 도움을 요청하는 것" (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) ask, can, for, from, help, people, trust, whom, you 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: ask for help from people whom you can trust
det.analysis:
'도움을 요청하다'는 ask for help로 나타내요. ask for는 '~을 요청하다'라는 뜻이에요.

'~로부터'는 from을 써서 from people(사람들로부터)로 이어요.

'당신이 신뢰할 수 있는 (사람들)'은 목적격 관계대명사 whom을 써서 뒤에서 꾸며요: people whom you can trust(당신이 신뢰할 수 있는 사람들). whom은 뒤 절에서 trust의 목적어 역할을 해요.

순서대로 이으면 ask / for / help / from / people / whom / you / can / trust.
det.tip: ask for help = 도움을 요청하다 / people whom you can trust = 목적격 관계대명사 whom

questions.wa: ask for help from people whom you can trust
accept: ask for help from people whom you can trust

questions.passage: To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience.  Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground.  If you are resilient, __________ you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity.  So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.  There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth.  Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"당신은 힘든 시간들로부터 다시 튀어 올라 빠르게 회복할 수 있다."

[ and / back / bounce / can / from / hard / quickly / recover / the / times / you ] (11단어) (영어로)

det.korean: you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times
det.analysis:
주어 'you(당신은)'로 시작하고, '~할 수 있다'를 뜻하는 조동사 can을 이어요: you can.

'다시 튀어 오르다'는 bounce back이에요. 조동사 can 뒤라서 동사원형 bounce를 써요.

'빠르게 회복하다'는 and로 이어 recover quickly로 나타내요. bounce와 recover가 can 뒤에서 나란히 연결돼요(병렬).

'힘든 시간들로부터'는 from the hard times예요.

순서대로 이으면 you / can / bounce / back / and / recover / quickly / from / the / hard / times.
det.tip: bounce back = 다시 튀어 오르다(회복탄력성의 핵심 표현) / can 뒤 동사원형 병렬: bounce ~ and recover

questions.wa: you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times
accept: you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times

"나는 이 전략들이 쉽다고 말하고 있는 것이 아니다" (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) am, are, easy, I, not, saying, strategies, that, these 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: I am not saying that these strategies are easy
det.analysis:
'나는 ~라고 말하고 있는 것이 아니다'는 현재진행형의 부정 'I am not saying'으로 나타내요. be동사 am 뒤에 not을 넣고 -ing(saying)를 이어요.

말하는 내용은 접속사 that이 이끄는 명사절로 나타내요: that these strategies are easy(이 전략들이 쉽다는 것).

that절 안에서 주어는 these strategies(이 전략들)로 복수이고, 동사는 복수형 are, 보어는 easy(쉬운)예요.

순서대로 이으면 I / am / not / saying / that / these / strategies / are / easy.
det.tip: I am not saying that ~ = 나는 ~라고 말하는 것이 아니다 (현재진행 부정 + that절)

questions.wa: I am not saying that these strategies are easy
accept: I am not saying that these strategies are easy
